skeleton:
Higher-Protein Full English Breakfast

British · Easy · Serves 1

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The full English re-weighted for the training table: same architecture, same browned-and-buttered character, with the protein components doubled and the starch-and-sugar slots quietly reassigned. A classic full English runs roughly 25–30 g of protein; this plate runs 50 g and upwards, without becoming a bodybuilder's joke — the eggs get an extra, the bacon doubles, the sausage stays, black pudding adds its iron and protein, and the beans go from garnish to a proper protein-bearing pool. The hash brown's slot goes to the crispy breakfast potato cubes at half portion, or disappears on the strictest day. The design principle is honest: the fry-up's pleasures are fat, salt, and crust, and this plate keeps all three while shifting the calorie share from toast-and-beans toward egg-and-meat. It is still a full English — it smells like one, eats like one, and the plate still needs a mug of tea beside it.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The protein core

  • 3 for the plate, 3 for a soft scramble stacked alongside (or 4 fried and 2 whites folded into the scramble)
  • grilled or pan-crisped

The re-weighted supports

  • or none, on the strict day

To finish

- **The egg maths is the plate's backbone:** 3 fried eggs (18 g protein) + a 3-egg soft scramble folded with the extra whites (24 g) + 6 rashers of back bacon (30 g) + 2 sausages (14 g) + black pudding (10 g) + beans (8 g) crosses 100 g of protein before the potato counts. For the moderate version, 4 eggs and 4 rashers lands around 70 g. Choose the day's arithmetic before cooking. - **The scramble runs alongside, not instead:** the extra eggs cook as the creamy chive scrambled eggs' firmer café version — medium heat, curds set soft-dry — and land as a second mound beside the fried eggs. Two egg preparations on one plate is not excess; it is the plate's architecture showing its re-weighting. - Sequence: oven tray (tomato, mushrooms, potato cubes) runs parallel to the pan (sausages, bacon, pudding), scramble last.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • Tray: tomato jammy, mushrooms browned, cubes crisp.
  • Pan: sausages clear-juiced, bacon glassy-flat, pudding crusted — one pan, one fat economy.
  • Eggs: three basted with running yolks plus a distinct soft-curd scramble.
  • Assembly: hot together, protein-dense, still unmistakably a full English.

Higher-Protein Full English Breakfast

Prep: 10 minutes · Cook: 25 minutes · Total: 35 minutes · Serves 1

Ingredients

The protein core

  • 6 large eggs (330 g) — 3 for the plate, 3 for a soft scramble stacked alongside (or 4 fried and 2 whites folded into the scramble)
  • 6 rashers (300 g) back bacon — grilled or pan-crisped
  • 2 good pork sausages (160 g)
  • 2 thick slices (150 g) black pudding

The re-weighted supports

  • 150 g quick stovetop breakfast beans (protein-bearing, sauce-clinging)
  • 100 g crispy breakfast potato cubes (the half portion) — or none, on the strict day
  • 1 large tomato (150 g), halved and grilled
  • 100 g chestnut mushrooms, halved

To finish

  • 15 g butter
  • 5 ml / 5 g olive oil
  • 2 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g black pepper
  • 10 g chives, snipped

Instructions

  1. **The tray stage — 15 minutes at 200 °C.** Tomato half and mushrooms roasted with the oil, salt, and pepper; the potato cubes run their par-boil-and-crisp sequence (or re-crisp from a batch) on the same tray. Checkpoint — tomato slumped and jammy; mushrooms browned; cubes deep-gold and rattling-crisp on two faces minimum.
  2. **The pan stage — sausages, bacon, pudding.** Sausages 12 minutes over medium-low to browned and clear-juiced; bacon added for the last 6, pressed flat to glassy fat; black pudding crusted for the final 4. Checkpoint — all three meats browned in sequence in the one pan, the fat economy running as ever, everything holding heat on the warm plate while the eggs stage begins.
  3. **The fried eggs — 3, basted, 3 minutes.** Three eggs into the pan's fat, basted to set whites and liquid yolks, lace edges. Checkpoint — whites set, yolks running — three of them, crowning the plate in a row.
  4. **The scramble — 4 minutes, parallel.** While the fried eggs run, beat the remaining 3 eggs (with the 2 extra whites if using) and scramble them in a second pan over medium heat with the butter, stirring constantly to small, soft-set curds — the café firm-soft, not the creamy run-off-heat version, so the two egg preparations read differently on the plate. Chives through at the end. Checkpoint — the scramble holds soft defined curds with no wetness pooling — distinct from the fried eggs' runny yolks, a second texture on the same plate.
  5. **Assemble the re-weighted plate.** Fried eggs at the crown, scramble beside in its mound, bacon fanned, sausages and black pudding flanking, beans and potato cubes at the sides, tomato and mushrooms filling. Checkpoint — the plate is visibly heftier than the classic — two egg preparations, double bacon — and every component is hot together. The mug of builder's tea arrives because the plate asked.

Finish & Plate

Brown sauce sparingly — the plate is seasoned enough. Tea, black coffee, or both. On training days this is the breakfast that replaces the shaker; on rest days, halve the scramble and the bacon and the plate reads as a hearty classic. The point was never maximalism — it was that the full English's architecture could carry any brief without losing its soul.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Scramble rubberyHigh heat or held too longMedium, constant stir, off-heat pull
Plate cold by the second egg batchNo parallel stagingTray and pan run together; eggs last, always
Felt like a food-shop macro sheet, not breakfastBeans skipped or tomato skippedThe supports are what make it a fry-up; keep the plate's identity
Sausages undercooked insideHigh heat, plump linksMedium-low and patient, clear juices at a nick

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **The meats and beans batch-cook well** (3 days refrigerated); the eggs cook fresh each morning — the 6-minute weekday version is reheated meats plus fresh basted eggs. - **Variation — the lean build:** all bacon trimmed, vegetarian sausages, 4 eggs, potato slot cut — a lower-fat plate that keeps the architecture. - **Variation — the smoked salmon bridge:** the scramble folded with 80 g smoked salmon at the end — protein and the full English's coastal cousin in one move. - **The honest note:** no powder, no substitute, no apology — the plate reaches its numbers with the fry-up's own ingredients, which is the only way a full English agrees to any of this.
